sources.title: Ctenanthe
sources.clean:
Ctenanthe is a genus of flowering plants of the family Marantaceae described as a genus in 1884. They are evergreen perennials, native to Central and South America (primarily Brazil). They are grown for their attractive, often variegated foliage. They are frost tender, requiring a minimum temperature of {{convert|13|C|0|abbr=on}}.

 Species 

The genus has the following species:
{{columns-list|colwidth=30em|
* ''[[Ctenanthe amabilis]]'' - Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe amphiandina]]'' - Ecuador, Peru, NW Brazil, Colombia, Bolivia
* ''[[Ctenanthe burle-marxii]]'' - [[Espírito Santo]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe casupoides]]'' - E + S Brazil, [[Misiones Province|Misiones]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe compressa]]'' - Venezuela, Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe dasycarpa]]'' - Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia
* ''[[Ctenanthe ericae]]'' - SE Colombia, Ecuador, [[Acre (state)|Acre]], [[Rondônia]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe glabra]]'' - Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe kummerana]]'' - [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe lanceolata]]'' - S + SE Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe lubbersiana]]'' - [[Minas Gerais]], [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe marantifolia]]'' - SE Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe muelleri]]'' - S + SE Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe oppenheimiana]]'' - [[Bahia]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe setosa]]'' - S + E Brazil
}}

 Awards 

The Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit has been awarded to the following:
Ctenanthe amabilis
Ctenanthe lubbersiana (common name: bamburanta), which grows to {{convert|2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} and bears large, oval leaves up to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, heavily striped and mottled with yellow
Ctenanthe oppenheimiana 'Tricolor' (common name "never-never plant"), which grows to {{convert|2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} with narrow, oval leaves up to {{convert|40|cm|0|abbr=on}} long with V-shaped silver patterns above and maroon below.
